bloom: this format has no Bloom filter (pages route by chained fences and the learned model); nothing to zero
not_applicable: truncated_blob baseline: the baseline reads no code (code is one read, made in the path mode only), so no blob is fetched

faults.name: none
faults.description: control: responses pass through untouched

faults.name: node_omitted
faults.description: the page holding the aimed node re-encoded without it; fences and count stay consistent, so the node is silently missing

faults.name: page_malformed
faults.description: the page holding the aimed node re-encoded without it but the header's count left as it was: the offset table no longer matches

faults.name: forged_fence
faults.description: the page the model predicts for the aimed node, when that is not the page holding it, re-encoded with fences [0^32, FF^32]: it claims to cover the node, so the node is found absent from it instead of on its neighbour (a node the model predicts exactly cannot be misrouted this way, and is aimed past)

faults.name: fence_gap
faults.description: the page holding the aimed node re-encoded with fences narrowed to its first entry and the successor of its last: keys in the former gaps fall between pages, but every node a walk needs is an entry and stays covered, so this cannot misroute a read (a negative control). A page whose fences are already that tight cannot be narrowed and is aimed past: in the pre-order account table a node's nibble-0 child has the node's key plus one, so a page that ends on a node and is followed by its 0-child (page 1, holding the root, always is) has no gap

faults.name: fence_excludes
faults.description: the page holding the aimed node re-encoded with its upper fence lowered onto its last entry, so a key the page holds is outside its fences; the page's own validation rejects it (not aimable on the table's last page, whose upper fence must stay FF^32)

faults.name: truncated_page
faults.description: the range response holding the aimed node's page answered with half the bytes asked

faults.name: truncated_latest
faults.description: snapshots/latest answered with its first half
faults.open_error: latest is not a block hash

baseline.open_error: latest is not a block hash

path.open_error: latest is not a block hash

faults.name: truncated_manifest
faults.description: the manifest answered with its first half (latest served whole)
faults.open_error: EOF while parsing an object at line 22 column 18

baseline.open_error: EOF while parsing an object at line 22 column 18

path.open_error: EOF while parsing an object at line 22 column 18

faults.name: truncated_blob
faults.description: blob files answered with their first half

baseline.not_applicable: the baseline reads no code (code is one read, made in the path mode only), so no blob is fetched

faults.name: wrong_run_page
faults.description: in the range response holding the aimed node's page, that page replaced by one whole data page of another table (account_nodes from storage_nodes and back, nodes_by_hash from code and back; the same page number modulo the other table's page count), the rest of the response intact

faults.name: wrong_range
faults.description: the range response holding the aimed node's page answered from one page further into the same file

faults.name: bit_flip
faults.description: unaimed: one random bit flipped in every data range response

faults.name: bit_flip_page
faults.description: one random bit flipped in the page holding the aimed node

faults.name: model_page_tamper
faults.description: one random bit flipped in each model page record

faults.name: page0_tamper
faults.description: one random bit flipped in page 0 (header and top model) of every table

faults.name: page0_missing
faults.description: page 0 of every table answered Ok(None): no table can route

faults.name: manifest_state_root
faults.description: manifest state_root altered

faults.name: manifest_model_root
faults.description: every table's model_root in the manifest altered

faults.name: manifest_table_root
faults.description: every table's root (blake3 of the run file) in the manifest altered; the client never checks it, the trie proves values

faults.name: missing_range
faults.description: the range response holding the aimed node's page answered Ok(None) (the host says the file is not there); page 0 and model pages are served, so the refusal lands mid-walk

faults.name: http_error
faults.description: the range response holding the aimed node's page answered Err(500); page 0 and model pages are served, so the refusal lands mid-walk

faults.name: stale_value
faults.description: the aimed node's value bytes altered in place (one byte), the page re-encoded

faults.name: stale_page
faults.description: every entry's value bytes altered in place on the page holding the aimed node
